main_question: How do satellite AI and conventional methods compare in mapping new flood events, and how does the choice of pre-flood reference affect their performance?
central_contribution: model–information complementarity in applied flood mapping; error/coverage and preparation-resource trade-offs
reference_policies: P1 updated compatible pre-event reference under a source-fixed label-blind policy
policy_operation: replace the one pre-image; hold event image and trained weights fixed; no third-image fusion architecture
source_dataset: all5,000 held radar-change records/20events, known water-containing conditioning retained
source_fit_reuse: only exact compatible source fits; no unconditional restart of completed studies
evaluation_census: all eligible released records of the declared independent cohort and all assessable local radar cases; repeated AOIs/acquisitions remain dependent
local_case_role: Dutch/German receiving-case error and acquisition-timing interpretation; existing labels inspected before this design, not new confirmatory independent floods
gauge_data_role: event timing and measurement context, not pixel-inundation truth or a new discharge model
writing_scale: one substantial empirical article; approximately30–40main thesis-format pages plus necessary appendix, descriptive allowance not requirement
